name: Rolandic epilepsy-paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia-writer's cramp syndrome
aliases: Rolandic epilepsy with paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia and writer's cramp

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for Rolandic epilepsy-paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia-writer's cramp syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of centrotemporal (rolandic) epileptic seizures characterized by focal motor seizures with orofacial involvement
Episodes of dystonia triggered by prolonged or intense physical exercise
Task-specific focal hand dystonia manifesting as writer's cramp
Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions
Family history of epilepsy or dystonia supportive but not mandatory

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: rolandic epilepsy seizures, paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia, and writer's cramp
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not definitive.

searchTerms: seizure affecting one side of face
EEG showing sharp waves in parietal area
brain wave spikes in parietal lobe

common.symptomName: EEG with parietal focal spike waves
searchTerms: EEG with focal spike waves in parietal region
parietal lobe spike activity on EEG
localized brain spikes in parietal area

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of dystonia
imaging: Normal brain MRI without structural abnormalities
other: EEG showing centrotemporal spikes during wakefulness or sleep

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia and writer's cramp
Dystonia triggered by sudden movement rather than prolonged exercise
Writer's cramp without epileptic seizures or exercise-induced dystonia
